     1	# Brief: GitHub-native records with a durable local fallback
     2	
     3	> **SUPERSEDED.** This brief specified the original write-through design. The
     4	> owner reset the overbuilt first implementation of it (see
     5	> `results/telemetry/events.md`, 2026-09-01, and the archived branch
     6	> `telemetry/issue-0007-overbuilt`), and the shipped port is the lean
     7	> GitHub-only layer described in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`. Where this
     8	> brief and the shipped code disagree, the shipped code and protocol win. The
     9	> body below is unchanged: it is historical input, kept as research data.
    10	
    11	Issue: `#0007`
    12	Target branch: `issue-0007-github-native-workflow`
    13	Expected PR title: `feat(local): add GitHub write-through records`
    14	
    15	## Objective
    16	
    17	Implement the 2026-08-31 owner decision recorded in `HANDOFF.md` step 0 and
    18	`local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`: GitHub becomes the ordinary issue and pull
    19	request surface for `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, while the existing committed
    20	registry remains a complete write-through record and an offline fallback.
    21	
    22	Local CI and review continue to execute on this server. The local same-head
    23	manifest, verdict, and merge gate remain authoritative. The GitHub adapter
    24	publishes those results; it must not weaken, duplicate, or replace the gate.
    25	
    26	This is workflow work only. Do not modify Lean, blueprint, or paper-source
    27	content.
    28	
    29	## Sources to read first
    30	
    31	1. `HANDOFF.md`, especially immediate step 0.
    32	2. `local/personas/main.md`.
    33	3. `local/README.md`, `local/DESIGN.md`, and `local/protocols/meta.md`.
    34	4. `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`, `ci.md`, `review.md`, `sessions.md`, and
    35	   `build-cache.md`.
    36	5. The 2026-08-31 re-hybridization entry in `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
    37	6. `results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md` and issue `#0007`.
    38	7. Every script named in the scope below and the shared data layer in
    39	   `local/bin/track.py`.
    40	
    41	Use the GitHub REST documentation for issues, sub-issues, pull requests,
    42	commit statuses, and pull-request reviews. The relevant fine-grained token
    43	permissions are Issues write, Pull requests write, Commit statuses write, and
    44	Contents write.
    45	
    46	## Operator decisions
    47	
    48	These points are adjudicated. Do not leave them as OPEN items.
    49	
    50	### 1. Authority and degraded mode
    51	
    52	- GitHub is the normal human-facing record after this change lands.
    53	- Local issue and PR files are always written and remain sufficient to run the
    54	  local lifecycle while GitHub is unavailable.
    55	- A successful local mutation followed by a remote failure is not rolled back.
    56	  Record the remote operation as pending, print an actionable warning, and
    57	  leave enough state for deterministic reconciliation.
    58	- Default mode is best effort so a link outage does not stop formalization.
    59	  Provide an explicit required-online mode for operators/tests that need a
    60	  nonzero exit when GitHub synchronization fails.
    61	- `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_ENABLED=false` is the literal kill switch. Unset means
    62	  enabled, matching the existing kill-switch convention.
    63	- Never log tokens or copy authentication material into the repository.
    64	
    65	### 2. Identity and idempotency
    66	
    67	- Extend issue and PR records with optional GitHub identity and synchronization
    68	  fields. At minimum retain the GitHub number, URL, and whether synchronization
    69	  is `synced` or `pending`; retain the numeric GitHub issue id when needed for
    70	  the sub-issue API.
    71	- Do not use one coarse synchronization flag for the entire record. Store
    72	  pending/synced state beside the operation's durable local evidence: issue
    73	  object/state/parent operations with the issue record, PR object/post-merge
    74	  operations with the PR record, commit-status publication with the per-SHA CI
    75	  manifest or a same-directory sidecar, and review publication with a per-SHA
    76	  review sidecar. Reconciliation must be able to distinguish these operations
    77	  after a process dies between any two of them.
    78	- The per-entity operation journal must use deterministic keys and retain a
    79	  payload digest, prerequisites, state (`pending`, `applying`, `synced`,
    80	  `superseded`, or `conflict`), attempt count, relevant remote id, timestamps,
    81	  and a classified last error. Distinguish at least `issue.ensure`,
    82	  `issue.parent`, `pr.head`, `pr.ensure`, `ci:<sha>:<context>`,
    83	  `review:<sha>:<digest>`, and `merge.main:<merge-sha>`.
    84	- Seed the existing mappings from
    85	  `results/telemetry/github-migration-map.md`; never recreate those records.
    86	- Every remotely created object carries a hidden stable marker based on the
    87	  local id, for example `mipstarre-local-issue:0007` or
    88	  `mipstarre-local-pr:0004`.
    89	- Before every create attempt, and again after an ambiguous failure, search the
    90	  authoritative REST listing for the marker. Do not rely on eventually
    91	  consistent search indexing. Adopt a unique match; treat multiple matches as
    92	  a conflict requiring operator attention.
    93	- Repeated synchronization after success must be a no-op except for deliberate
    94	  field/body/state updates.
    95	
    96	### 3. Shared adapter and configuration
    97	
    98	- Put GitHub API, retry, identity, and reconciliation logic in one Python
    99	  adapter under `local/bin/`; do not duplicate ad hoc `gh` fragments across
   100	  shell scripts.
   101	- Invoke the REST API through `gh api`. Support an explicit executable override
   102	  such as `MIPSTARRE_GH` so deterministic tests can supply a fake CLI.
   103	- Resolve the repository from `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` or the `github` remote,
   104	  and retain `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A` as the documented default.
   105	- Retry bounded transient failures with short exponential backoff. Tests must
   106	  be able to set delays to zero.
   107	- Retry connection failures, timeouts, `429`, and `5xx`; retain permanent
   108	  authentication, validation, and other `4xx` failures as pending or conflict
   109	  without wasting the full retry budget.
   110	- Validate CLI presence and API capability separately. Use a harmless
   111	  authenticated API probe rather than trusting `gh auth status`: the installed
   112	  `gh 2.4.0` reports a valid fine-grained PAT as invalid even though
   113	  `gh api user` succeeds. Missing CLI, authentication, or connectivity is a
   114	  loud pending-sync state, not silent success and not loss of the local record.
   115	- Add an explicit reconciliation command that can sync one issue, one PR, or
   116	  all pending records. Reconciliation is the recovery path after an offline or
   117	  ambiguous operation.
   118	- This adapter does not import arbitrary human edits made directly on GitHub.
   119	  Lifecycle scripts remain the mutation entry points for tool-owned title,
   120	  body, label, state, and gate fields. Document that boundary rather than
   121	  inventing an implicit last-writer-wins policy.
   122	
   123	### 4. Issue lifecycle
   124	
   125	- `issue_new.py` allocates and completes the local create/classify/scout stages
   126	  first, then ensures the GitHub issue exists with the final title, body, and
   127	  labels.
   128	- Apply only labels that exist in the GitHub repository and report missing
   129	  labels; do not let one absent label abort issue creation.
   130	- Translate local parent identity through the stored mapping. After both
   131	  records exist, use GitHub's sub-issue endpoint to attach the child. A pending
   132	  parent leaves an explicit pending relation for reconciliation.
   133	- `issue_close.py` maps local `not-planned` to GitHub `not_planned` and preserves
   134	  `completed`. It must be safe to retry even when the local issue is already
   135	  closed.
   136	- Remote issue bodies may expose the local id, but generated cross-reference
   137	  footers must use mapped GitHub numbers so `#N` never points to an unrelated
   138	  issue or pull request.
   139	
   140	### 5. Pull-request publication and the empty-branch case
   141	
   142	- Preserve the current operating loop in which the local PR record may be
   143	  opened before the implementation commit exists.
   144	- Enforce one open local PR record per branch. A repeated invocation must reuse
   145	  or report the existing record rather than allocate a second local identity.
   146	- GitHub rejects a PR whose head has no commits ahead of its base. In that case
   147	  `pr_open.py` creates the local record, marks remote creation pending, and says
   148	  exactly why. It is not an error and must not manufacture a placeholder
   149	  commit.
   150	- Once the branch has a real head, reconciliation publishes the feature branch
   151	  and creates or updates the GitHub PR. `ci.sh` may ensure this publication
   152	  before posting its status.
   153	- Narrow the old push rule explicitly: feature branches may be pushed as PR
   154	  heads; GitHub `main` may advance only after the local merge gate passes.
   155	- Translate `Addresses`/`Closes` footers from local issue ids to mapped GitHub
   156	  issue numbers in the remote PR body.
   157	
   158	### 6. Same-head CI status
   159	
   160	- `ci.sh` publishes a stable context such as `MIPStarRE/local-ci` for the exact
   161	  `HEAD_SHA` in its manifest. Publish `pending` when the run begins and the
   162	  final `success`, `failure`, or `error` after the complete manifest is written.
   163	- Partial/debug runs must not publish a success status.
   164	- Before posting, ensure the commit exists in the remote repository. Never
   165	  attach a result to a different or merely current branch head.
   166	- Recheck the actual local branch tip immediately before final publication;
   167	  re-reading only `pr.md` is insufficient if a commit lands during CI.
   168	- An ambiguous status POST is reconciled by reading the latest status with the
   169	  same SHA and context before retrying.
   170	- A remote publication failure does not rewrite the local CI conclusion. It
   171	  leaves GitHub synchronization pending and is recoverable from the manifest.
   172	
   173	### 7. Same-head review publication
   174	
   175	- After `review.sh` writes its local verdict files and rechecks the final head,
   176	  publish one review summary tied explicitly to that `HEAD_SHA`.
   177	- The GitHub account that opens these PRs cannot approve its own PR. Therefore
   178	  publish a GitHub `COMMENT` review for every local verdict and state clearly
   179	  that `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED`, or `CHANGES_REQUESTED` is the local gate verdict.
   180	  Do not pretend a GitHub self-approval succeeded.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (changes) `local/protocols/issues-prs.md:22` — The authoritative prerequisite record still has no supported, adoption-safe write path in the issue lifecycle
- [ ] F4 (changes) `.githooks/pre-commit:41` — The new ready-packet workflow test remains outside the owner-gated infrastructure line budget

## Review

F1 remains unresolved. `issue_new.py` supports `--parent` but not prerequisite edges, while `gh_common.py` exposes no dependency mutation helper or CLI command. Once body bullets become commentary, operators cannot establish the authoritative record through the documented lifecycle. An ad hoc POST would also lack the required post-failure adoption check. Add a supported dependency mutation path and fake-API coverage.

F4 also remains unresolved. The hook budgets `local/`, `.githooks/`, and two explicitly named test files, excluding the new 137-line `test_ready_packets.py`. The current PR is only 330 changed lines including that test, so it is within budget; the defect is that future workflow changes can bypass enforcement through this file.

F2 is resolved by retaining closed dependency edges and testing that they remain recorded without blocking readiness. F3 is resolved by removing the unsupported orphan-detection claim. F5 is resolved: the corrected ranges enumerate exactly 35 direct tracker children.

The focused suite passes: 6 tests. `git diff --check` also passes. Full test discovery could not complete in the read-only reviewer sandbox because 252 existing tests require a writable temporary directory; exact-head local CI was reported green.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
